You are taking a test. It's either A, B, or C. You choose A completely at random. The teacher announces to class B is not the answer. The teacher does not know your answer. Should you switch to C?

Elsewhere the overwhelming most popular response is that this isn't equivalent to the MHP, that is, the test taker has no reason to switch - that the teacher doesn't know my answer changes things somehow. This seems wrong to me. My intuition is that the key probably modifying issue with the MPH is that Monty won't open the door with the correct answer. His knowledge of the answer is immaterial. As a further extension, the problem as stated wouldn't even occur if the teacher announced that the selected answer was wrong.

Am I wrong? If so, what might you tell me to help me better understand the issue?
Is this really an instance of the Monty Hall problem?

Lets say that there are a few more answers. A, B, C, D, E. You still choose A randomly, but now the teacher says that there was a mistake in printing the test and to disregard C D, and E. Do you still feel that you should now choose B?
I think so, but I'll write the simulation and get back to you. :-)
No reason to switch after being told that B was wrong. All that has happened is your odds or getting the correct answer has changed from 1/3 to 1/2. If you had picked B then switch of course.

The difference is that because the teacher doesn't know what answer you selected, (stochastically) one time in three s/he will tell you that the answer you selected is wrong. This isn't a possibility under MH. It skews the probabilities in the MHP, but not in your scenario.

All that matters is what I know, not the teacher or class. I hear the teacher say that B is not the answer. That reduces the probability of my guessing the correct answer to 1/2. Could be A or C, so i have a 1 out of 2 chance of getting it right. Now picking A or C gives me the same chance of getting it right, so doesn't matter which I pick. The MHP is only a problem to those who don't know about probabilities..
